note: The CANCELLATION law of the self-dispatched flowEvalTick chain. `🔒️tick-latch.json` says whether a tick may be armed; this says what an explicit cancelPreviewEval gesture does to work already in flight — in this process, in the geometry extension's process, and in the status object the preview window publishes. Language-agnostic: an implementation in any language must replay these sequences and answer the same statuses, the same emitted invocations and the same resumability.

laws.cancellableMeansWorkInFlight: `cancellable` is true whenever ANY work a cancel would stop is outstanding — a tessellation in flight, an extension answer outstanding on any window, or a scheduled tick. The tessellation ledger alone is not enough: an `evaluate` round trip admits no tessellation, so a ledger-only predicate reads `idle`/not-cancellable through the slowest half of a boolean preview.
laws.cancelFreezesProgress: A cancel stamps `phase: "cancelled"` and leaves unitsDone/unitsTotal/facesDone/facesTotal exactly where they were. Progress is evidence of work already paid for; a cancel retires the work, never the record of it.
laws.cancelIsNotCancellable: Once cancelled, nothing is left to stop, so `cancellable` is false until work resumes.
laws.cancelReachesTheExtensionActor: The kernel jobs live in the geometry extension's own wasm instance behind its own process-global registries, so the guest's linked copies are always empty from the app's side. The gesture therefore emits exactly TWO invocations addressed at the geometry extension — `evaluateCancel` for the parked budgeted operator evaluations and `tessellateCancel` for the mesh jobs — both answering on `flowTessellateCancelResolve`. Two doors, because there are two registries and each names its own; a boolean stopped mid-validation is in the first and in neither of the others.
laws.unaddressableKernelEmitsNothing: An unaddressable geometry extension has no actor to tell; the local half of the cancel still happens and no invocation is emitted.
laws.cancelQuiescesTheLatch: Every window's arming latch falls back to armed=false, inFlight=0, owed=false, unfinished=false. Removing the latch outright would make the host refresh poll read `this window never ticked` and re-arm the very chain the user stopped.
laws.noStaleChunksSurviveACancel: The half-received mesh body AND the chunk cursor that addresses it are dropped together. Keeping the cursor makes the next evaluation of the same handle ask for chunk n and concatenate it onto nothing — a silently truncated pack body.
laws.aLaterGestureResumes: Only a gesture resumes a cancelled chain. The first tick that actually begins clears the cancelled banner.
laws.everyPreviewWindowPublishesTheContract: The status object is a property of a World3d PREVIEW WINDOW, not of a surface: all three of them — the editor's edit-mode preview, the editor's generate-mode generation preview and the viewer's read-only preview — publish the identical schema from the identical projection. A window that renders meshes while publishing no phase/progress/cancellable is the defect this section exists to forbid: the user can watch nothing and stop nothing, and the shell has no cancelAction to declare.
laws.theCancelVerbIsLearnedFromTheStatus: The shell never learns the cancel verb from code — it reads `cancelAction` off the published status and declares it for exactly as long as `cancellable` holds. A surface that publishes the contract must therefore also DECLARE that command in its manifest, or the gesture is dropped by the host's declaredAction gate before the app ever sees it.
laws.aSessionlessWindowStillPublishes: A preview window rendered without a retained evaluation session (a surface's marks-free render entry point) publishes the SAME schema with idle phase, zero progress and nothing to cancel. Publishing nothing is never an option.

rows.why: The headline case: two handles admitted, one step folded, then the user stops it.
A cancel raised before any tessellation was admitted — the ledger has no row to stamp, so a ledger-only status would publish `idle` and swallow the gesture.
A multi-chunk transfer stopped halfway. The next evaluation must ask for chunk 0 again.
The gesture is a state, not a delta.
The in-flight request the host had already sent still answers. It must not revive the chain.

hostDoor.note: The host half. `driveInboundRequest` reads its AbortSignal at TURN BOUNDARIES, so a cancel retires a parked multi-turn request and never half-abandons a turn already handed to the worker. `PluginWasmHandle.invoke` forwards `context.signal` into it; the shell registers one AbortController per in-flight extension request, keyed by the REQUESTING actor, and the surface's declared cancel action aborts that actor's set.

statusContract.note: The status object every World3d preview window publishes on `World3dScene.statusJson`, in the four states a preview can be in. Language-agnostic: an implementation in any language must reach the same object from the same session sequence.
statusContract.ratioLaw: ratio = (unitsDone + chunksDone) / (unitsTotal + chunksTotal); a zero total is 1 when nothing is in flight and 0 otherwise.

states.why: Nothing admitted and nothing in flight. The contract is still published, in full — this is the state the viewer preview used to publish as nothing at all.
Two handles admitted, one step folded: work a cancel would stop, so the affordance is offered.
A CONTRIBUTED geometry extension that refuses an evaluate. The live fault outranks the ledger phase and retires the affordance.
No loaded plugin contributes the geometry extension, so nothing was ever invoked: the ledger's idle is a lie the surface cannot act on.
The gesture outranks the ledger and freezes the progress already paid for.
